**3 stars — great fitout, rough October.**

Full transparency up front: I run a mobile grooming van (Fluff Bus Mobile Grooming, Halifax) and had Harbourline do the whole build in August — stainless tub and ramp, fresh and grey tanks, on-demand propane hot water, plumbing, cabinetry and coin-grip floor. $9,400 + HST on the invoice.

The tub and ramp are honestly the best part of the van. Dogs walk right in, the ramp is solid, and the tub cleans up beautifully. Other groomers reading this: the tub alone is worth it. If you get one thing from this review, get the tub.

But this is 3 stars and not 5 because of October 27.

Mid-groom, the compression fitting on the hot water line let go. Water everywhere, down into the cabinet, across the floor, the van flooded out. I was in Bedford at the time with Moose, a 110 lb Bernese Mountain Dog, sitting in the tub. Here's the thing — Moose sat in that tub through the entire flood like he was at a spa. Didn't move, didn't flinch, looked at me like I was the one being ridiculous. I was the one screaming and grabbing towels. His owner Carole has since told me he went home looking like a wet sheepdog and has apparently never been happier; he thought it was a pool party. Meanwhile I had to towel him off and send him home half-done, cancel the rest of that day, and lose six bookings over the following week while the van sat off the road from Oct 27 to Nov 6.

That was the part that actually cost me. Not the leak — stuff breaks, water happens, that's normal and it's on me to keep on top of my rig. What made me mad was being told it was user error before anyone had looked at it.

When it first happened, Glenn's initial reply was that fittings like that don't just let go, usually the heater's been run dry or someone has hung something off the pipe, and that would be user error and not covered. I get where he was coming from, and to be fair I did push back on that reply. But I have never run it dry and nothing hangs off that pipe — it's behind a cabinet door. If your livelihood depends on this van, hearing "that's on you" before a single wrench has been turned is a rotten feeling, especially when you're standing in a flooded van with a soaking wet dog in front of you.

Credit where it's due, because he earned it: Glenn found the actual cause — a cheaper compression fitting his own supplier had swapped in — owned it, replaced all of the fittings on the hot side, and knocked the $180 diagnostic fee off as goodwill. No argument, no runaround. That's exactly what I wanted from the start and he did it. He also mentioned he keeps an eye on the reviews here and that he'll be reading this, so let me be clear: there's nothing personal in any of this. Glenn's a decent operator, the build was good, and when the cause turned out to be on his side he stepped up and said so.

So, advice for any other groomer or trade looking at them: get the warranty terms in writing before you pay. The invoice says a 12-month workmanship warranty that excludes damage from misuse or user error. That's a normal and fair concept, but "user error" is carrying a lot of weight in that sentence. Ask exactly what's excluded. Ask who covers the fittings and the plumbing. Ask what the diagnostic fee is and whether it gets credited if it turns out to be their fault. Mine wasn't written down anywhere, and my first call back was "that's user error." Write it down.

Overall: excellent build, great tub and ramp, and the repair was handled properly once the cause was found. The October outage cost me real bookings and real money, and the first response could have been less "your fault." Three stars — I'd happily recommend the fitout, but get the warranty details in writing and don't take anyone's first guess as the diagnosis.
